High-level ask: can Redwood support an initial trial with ~8 concurrent request slots, average 300 tokens per request, peak bursts up to 1,200 tokens for a handful of sessions? We're evaluating whether to run this on Hosted API or request temporary Dedicated capacity for the workshop.

Proposed windows (Pacific):
- Tue 20 Apr, 10:00-12:00
- Thu 22 Apr, 14:00-16:00
- Mon 25 Apr, 11:00-13:00 (preferred)

Let me know what you need from us to confirm (prompt sets, expected RPS, sample payloads). Also please loop in whoever owns capacity/quotas.

Cheers,

Nimbus Capital

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-19T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC workshop + quick capacity question

Hi all — quick technical readout to make scheduling concrete.

Assumptions we need confirmed from Nimbus before final sizing:
- Sustained RPS (avg): 8 requests/sec or 8 concurrent sessions? (these are different for batching efficiency)
- Typical request token distribution: mean 300, p95 ~900, max ~1,200 (you mentioned bursts)
- KV cache hit rate expectation (do you reuse prompt prefixes across many users?)

For the workshop planning: if sustained load is ~8 RPS with mean 300 tokens, Hosted with a temporary quota bump + aggressive batching should be fine for the hands-on run. If you expect many simultaneous 1,200-token requests, Dedicated is safer — it avoids noisy-neighbor rate shaping during the experiment.

Proposed technical checklist for the workshop:
- We provision a Hosted quota bump: token budget 500k tokens for the session window, temp QPS increase to 50 (30-minute rolling).
- Prepare a Dedicated fallback: single GPU pool pre-warmed with model v1.2-quant that supports 1,200-token bursts.
- Load test plan: 3 stages (ramp, steady-state, burst). We'll run a short 10-min steady-state at target load, then 2 x 2-min bursts at peak to validate tail latency.

I'm attaching a quick capacity worksheet (capacity_estimates_nimbus.xlsx) and will draft the exact curl/sim scripts for the prompt_set_v1.txt you sent.

—Dev
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Grant <sophie@nimbuscapital.com>

Thanks, Dev — good clarifications. Answers below:
- Sustained load: 8 concurrent user sessions (roughly translates to 6–8 RPS during active periods).
- Token distribution: mean ~300, p95 ~950, max ~1,200 for heavy dialogs (approx 15% of requests).
- KV cache: moderate reuse across workflows; expect ~40–50% prefix reuse.

We are happy to try Hosted with your quota bump approach and keep the Dedicated pool as fallback. Mon 25 Apr 11:00-13:00 PT works for our team — please send calendar invite.

Two asks before the session:
1) Can Redwood request a temporary token quota bump and a QPS increase for our trial org?
2) Will someone run the load scripts and share the latency/cost breakdown in real-time during the workshop?

Appreciate it — Sophie
